title: API 580 Training in Newark: Risk Based Inspection Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 580 exam prep for North Jersey RBI teams: refinery and chemical plant data, New Jersey rules that limit RBI intervals, instructor Q&A.
h1: API 580 Risk Based Inspection Exam Prep for Newark-Area Refinery, Chemical and Terminal Teams
html:
API 580 exam prep for risk-based inspection teams around Newark Bay

Risk-based inspection in North Jersey is shaped by rules as much as by risk. The Bayway complex in Linden puts a refinery, an additive maker, an acid regenerator, a cogeneration plant and a fuel terminal side by side; the harbor terminals at Bayonne, Carteret and Perth Amboy hold millions of barrels in storage tanks; and New Jersey adds its own pressure vessel, discharge prevention and toxic catastrophe rules on top of the federal ones. An inspection planner who sits API 580 here needs RP 580's concepts and a clear sense of where they can and cannot be applied.

Atlantis NDT's API 580 course is self-paced exam preparation, online, with an instructor answering questions as you work through API RP 580 and the damage-mechanism and inspection ideas behind it. There is no Atlantis classroom in Newark. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility, administers the API 580 examination and issues the certification. API's programme page describes a closed-book exam of 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 of them scored, lasting 3.25 hours, that can be scheduled at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring. The 2026 Body of Knowledge bases it on RP 580, 4th Edition (August 2023) with Addendum 1 (March 2025).

Who sits API 580 in North Jersey

  • Owner-user inspectors who already hold API 510, 570 or 653, qualify for API 580 automatically and want to read RBI output critically rather than take it on trust.
  • Inspection planners and reliability engineers at refinery and chemical sites who turn RBI results into inspection plans.
  • Corrosion and materials engineers who supply damage mechanism reviews and corrosion rates to an RBI team.
  • Terminal integrity coordinators who need to know what RBI can and cannot do for regulated storage tanks.
  • Process safety staff who run mechanical integrity programmes under federal and state process safety rules.

Without a current 510, 570 or 653 certificate, API counts education plus petrochemical industry experience in the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, two with a two-year degree or certificate, three with a high school diploma and five or more with no formal education. Because API asks for petrochemical industry experience rather than inspection experience for this certificate, process and reliability engineers at additive, polymer or acid regeneration plants may qualify on the degree route; API decides whether a given role counts.

Four rules that decide where an RBI interval can be used

An RBI programme does not set aside jurisdictional requirements; it has to work inside them. In New Jersey those limits differ by equipment type, and a planner who maps every asset to its regulatory driver before running the model saves a great deal of rework.

RuleEquipment it reachesEffect on RBI-based intervals
N.J.A.C. 12:90-5.14 and 12:90-5.19Unfired pressure vesselsVessels under a registered owner-user agency are inspected at the intervals the National Board Inspection Code or API 510 requires, and API 510 provides for intervals based on an RBI assessment. Vessels outside an owner-user agency get a state certificate inspection every three years.
N.J.A.C. 7:1E-2.16Aboveground tanks over 2,000 gallons at major facilitiesIntegrity testing follows API 653 for atmospheric steel tanks and API 510 or ASME Section VIII for pressurised ones, without the similar-service or risk-based scheduling options of API 653 and API 510.
49 CFR 195.432Pipeline breakout tanksAtmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks are inspected to API 653 except its section 6.4.3, so risk-based procedures cannot set the internal interval. A PHMSA proposal published in June 2026 would allow risk-based methods, but it is a proposed rule, not a final one.
40 CFR 68.73 and N.J.A.C. 7:31-4.5Covered process equipment, including vessels, tanks, piping and relief systemsFrequencies must be consistent with manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practice and tightened when experience calls for it; New Jersey adds a record system able to analyse inspection data to set frequencies. A documented RBI programme is one recognised way to meet that.

None of these rules appears on the exam. They matter because RP 580 questions about scope, objectives and the limits of an assessment are easier to answer once you have seen how a regulator can fix the "when" while leaving the "what" and "how" to the owner.

Mechanical integrity records as the raw material of RBI

New Jersey's Toxic Catastrophe Prevention Act rules, N.J.A.C. 7:31, set out the minimum requirements for a Program 3 TCPA risk management program, and two of their sections speak directly to an RBI team. Section 7:31-4.2 calls for process hazard analysis with risk assessment for specific pieces of equipment that handle extraordinarily hazardous substances. Section 7:31-4.5 adds to the federal mechanical integrity rule a requirement to keep accurate records of inspections, breakdowns, repairs and replacements, with the means of data retrieval and analysis needed to decide inspection and test frequencies and to evaluate equipment reliability.

That reads almost like a specification for the data an RBI assessment consumes. The RP 580 knowledge areas on data collection, damage mechanisms, the RBI team and documentation come more easily to candidates who have handled real inspection histories: thickness data by condition monitoring location, past inspection reports and how effective each one was, failure and repair records, and the process conditions that govern each mechanism. Where records are thin, sound RBI practice is to make conservative assumptions and write them down, so the next reassessment knows which inputs were guesses.

Probability and consequence on a shared industrial shore

Probability of failure at a refinery such as Bayway depends on the things RP 580 describes anywhere: active damage mechanisms, their rates, and how effective past inspections were at detecting them. Process changes deserve particular attention. OPIS reported in August 2026 that Phillips 66 was substituting domestic US crude grades for Brent-linked crude at Bayway; a change of feed is the kind of process change that should send an RBI team back to its assessment, because sulfur, acid and chloride content feed the hot-section and overhead mechanisms.

Consequence of failure has a local shape too. Consequence analysis weighs safety and health, environmental and business effects, and a North Jersey site meets all three in its own way: neighbours close to the fence line in a densely built state, tidal waterways such as the Arthur Kill and Newark Bay beside many tanks and docks, and, inside the Bayway complex, shared utilities such as steam from the cogeneration plant, so that an outage on one company's equipment can affect a neighbour's operations. No exam question names a site, but candidates who think in these terms find consequence questions easier.

A closed-book exercise: which rule sets the interval?

Many RP 580 questions describe a situation and ask what should happen next. Try this one with North Jersey equipment types. The answers follow the rules in the table above, not any particular site.

  1. A crude unit overhead accumulator at a refinery whose inspection department is a registered owner-user agency. An RBI assessment can set its interval, because the state accepts API 510 intervals and API 510 allows an RBI basis, provided the assessment is documented and kept current.
  2. A field-erected pressurised storage tank covered by N.J.A.C. 7:1E-2.16 at the same refinery. RBI can still rank it and target what is examined, but the integrity-test schedule comes from API 510 without its risk-based option.
  3. A gasoline tank at a harbor terminal covered by the same rule. The API 653 schedule applies, again without risk-based scheduling.
  4. A breakout tank on an interstate products pipeline. 49 CFR 195.432 excludes API 653's risk-based internal interval, so RBI informs priorities but cannot move the internal inspection date.
  5. Process piping in a TCPA-covered unit. A documented RBI programme can set CML inspection frequencies, provided it follows good engineering practice and the records show how each frequency was derived.

The pattern is the exam's real lesson. RBI decides what, where, how and when to inspect, and where a regulation fixes the when, the assessment still earns its keep on the other three.

Studying for a closed-book RBI exam from a North Jersey planning desk

The 2026 Body of Knowledge lists RP 580 and does not list RP 581, so the quantitative tables, damage factors and consequence calculations of RP 581 are background, not exam content. Its knowledge areas run from terms and definitions through risk assessment, the RBI programme, roles and qualifications, data collection, damage mechanisms, probability and consequence of failure and risk management to documentation. Because the whole exam is closed-book, the plan is about understanding and recall:

  1. Read RP 580 once from start to finish without notes, marking every term you use differently at work.
  2. Go back through it area by area with the instructor, asking how each concept maps onto the RBI software or spreadsheet your site uses.
  3. Learn enough damage-mechanism vocabulary to match mechanisms to inspection methods and to judge inspection effectiveness.
  4. Drill the definitions: probability of failure, consequence of failure, risk, risk driver, inspection effectiveness, mitigation and reassessment.
  5. Finish with timed practice papers at full exam length.

Exam preparation is not an RBI study

Passing API 580 shows you understand the concepts in RP 580. It does not make you the person who approves inspection intervals at a Linden plant; that authority sits with the owner's programme and, for vessels and piping, with the inspector and engineer roles the codes define. The course stays on the examination. Separately, Atlantis carries out remote RBI studies for owners, described on the New York Harbor RBI page; that is a different service from exam preparation, and fitness-for-service assessment is not part of it.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from a plant or terminal network

RBI works better when the people around the table share a vocabulary, so an employer might enrol an inspection planner, a corrosion engineer and one or two certified inspectors together. Employers can sponsor several candidates on one quote, and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API, chooses a test centre or remote proctoring where API offers it, and studies at their own pace with instructor Q&A. A terminal network with tanks under both the state discharge prevention rule and the federal breakout tank rule may want its integrity staff to understand exactly where RBI applies before they sit the exam, and those are good questions to take to the instructor in RP 580 terms.

faq.q: Do I need API 510, 570 or 653 before I can sit API 580?
faq.a: No. Holders of a current API 510, 570 or 653 certification qualify automatically, but you can also qualify on education plus petrochemical industry experience in the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, two with a two-year degree or certificate, three with a high school diploma, and five or more without formal education. The experience is documented on the application, and API decides.

faq.q: Can I take API 580 from home in Newark instead of at a test centre?
faq.a: The API 580 page on api.org says the exam can now be scheduled either at in-person test centres or through remote proctoring. Remote sessions come with their own rules on the room, the computer and identity checks, which API and its exam delivery provider set, so read them before you choose. If you prefer to sit in person, Prometric lists test centres in and around Newark.

faq.q: Can a New Jersey terminal use RBI to stretch its tank inspection dates?
faq.a: Not for tanks covered by N.J.A.C. 7:1E-2.16 at major facilities, where the rule applies API 653's schedule but not its similar-service or risk-based scheduling. Breakout tanks under 49 CFR 195.432 carry a similar restriction on the internal interval, and the PHMSA proposal published in June 2026 has not become a final rule. RBI can still rank tanks and target methods inside the required schedule.

faq.q: Does New Jersey's TCPA program require a risk-based inspection programme?
faq.a: Not as such. TCPA Program 3 requires a mechanical integrity and preventive maintenance programme on top of the federal rule, with records that can be retrieved and analysed to determine inspection and test frequencies. A documented RBI programme is one way of doing that analysis; code-based fixed intervals adjusted by experience are another. Which approach a site uses is the owner's decision, documented in its own procedures.

faq.q: Is API RP 581 on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: The 2026 Body of Knowledge names RP 580, 4th Edition with Addendum 1, as the publication examined and does not list RP 581. Quantitative ideas can appear at the level RP 580 discusses them, but you are not asked to work RP 581's damage factors or consequence calculations. Check the Body of Knowledge for your own window in case the list changes.

faq.q: Once I hold API 580, may I approve inspection intervals at a Linden plant?
faq.a: Not on the strength of the certificate alone. Who approves intervals is set by the owner's programme and the inspection codes; under API 510 and API 570 the inspector and engineer roles carry that responsibility, and New Jersey vessel records must identify the inspector's National Board Commission or API certification number. API 580 shows that you understand RBI; it does not replace those roles.

faq.q: How does a change of crude slate show up in an RBI programme?
faq.a: As a reason to reassess. Feed quality drives sulfidation, naphthenic acid corrosion, chloride-driven overhead corrosion and other mechanisms, so a team reviews the affected circuits and vessels, updates corrosion rates as new data arrives and checks that planned inspections still target the right mechanism. On the exam, recognise process change as a reassessment trigger and know which RBI inputs it touches.

faq.q: Can a chemical plant engineer with no inspection background sit API 580?
faq.a: Yes, if the experience is petrochemical industry experience gained in the last 10 years and long enough for the education held: one year with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology. Engineers at additive, polymer or acid regeneration plants should describe their roles clearly on the application. API decides whether the experience counts.
